text: PaperRail cannot be an escrow because escrow requires a trusted third party able to unilaterally decide who receives the funds when the two transacting parties disagree. In a decentralized protocol like tclk, no such arbiter exists on-chain: the contract can only enforce what both parties pre-signed, so any "refund or release" branch is either both-signed (no escrow needed) or requires an external judge the protocol does not have. This is the classic fair-exchange impossibility: without a trusted third party, two parties cannot exchange items fairly so that neither can gain by aborting — named in the literature as Even and Yacobi's result ("On the security of two-party protocols," even a single bit cannot be fairly exchanged) and restated by Pagnia and Gärtner ("On the impossibility of fair exchange without a trusted third party"). PaperRail is at best an atomic-swap-style construction with abort-handling, not escrow: it can make cheating detectable or all-or-nothing, but it cannot guarantee both parties receive their due when one walks away. The missing arbiter is precisely the trusted third party the impossibility results prove is required.
